Three things are needed before the day, and each ends in something that you can check: R and the workspace installed, with the setup check reporting no failure; the first module on R worked through; and the case study read. The day assumes that a linear model and its output are not new to you, and the readings at the end of this page prepare the statistics of the afternoon. The day itself is worked mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser with the data already in place, so a machine on which the installation failed can still follow every task.

## 1. R and the workspace

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the [workspace of the EU-frames case](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace), and run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure. Every fit of the menu then runs live on your machine. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met. If the installation will not cooperate, tell the facilitator before the day, and follow the day in the browser lab.

## 2. Getting started with R

[Open Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The module teaches the R that the browser lab asks of you, from a first line of code to a table and a figure. It works on the data of the housing-audit case, a file small enough to look at whole, and its blocks of code run in your browser.

## 3. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study, with its questions, data and selections, then SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses with an assessment of their choices, and how the results of the five analysts were put on one scale. Every part of the day works on this case.

## 4. The browser lab

[Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Open the lab once on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait until the R engine has loaded and the first cell shows a "Run Code" button, and run the three cells of Task 1. If they run, and the second reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, you are set. If it does not load, try another browser, and tell the facilitator before the day.

## 5. Further preparation

The [exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) sets out the claim and the table of what the five Multi100 analysts found: their recorded partial correlations run from −0.006 to −0.452, and working out how much of that spread comes from the analyses and how much from the conversion of their statistics takes up much of the day. The first sections of [Panel data](../../companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-aggregation), from the country-year level to clustered standard errors, read a first linear model on the panel output by output, and [Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) prepares Part 4. The modules on [the IDE (Positron and other IDEs)](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), on [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and on [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) take the tools of the workspace further.

**By the start of the day** you have the setup check reporting no failure, or the browser lab loading on the machine that you will use, you have worked through the first module on R, and you know how far apart the results of the five analysts are.
